<subject>RE: Update on TCO Bankruptcy Hearing and Producer Gas Usage</subject>
<body>
You should have the message below in your inbox regarding the producers on CGAS. Please respond once you confirm whether you can utilise the producer's gas without maintaining a minimum balance.

-----Original Message-----
From: Thompson, Laura  
Sent: Tuesday, 30 April 2002 16:09  
To: Harris, James; Bennett, Michael; Clarke, Sarah; Palmer, Emily  
Cc: O'Neill, Patrick; Davies, Helen; 'mark.evans@cwt.com'; 'sproctor@akllp.com'; Lewis, Daniel; Foster, Rachel; 'michael.koss@uk.pwcglobal.com'; 'jeffrey.benton@uk.pwcglobal.com'; Morgan, Adam  
Subject: Outcome of the TCO Bankruptcy Hearing Related to EES Matters

Here is a brief update on last week’s bankruptcy hearing for Columbia Gas Transmission (TCO) concerning the EES issues:

- TCO agreed to withdraw the part of their motion related to EES. The pipeline confirmed that EES has been utilising their transport contracts and has continued to pay invoices since the bankruptcy petition date.  
- The £1.5 million claim that TCO had previously included in the Halcyon "set off amount" (i.e., the outstanding demand charges for EES agreements through to contract expiry) has been removed from TCO’s motion.  
- The minimum OBA/pooling agreement monthly balance should no longer be required by the pipeline. (Note: Initially, TCO appeared to be using EES's minimum balance to offset Halcyon & EES obligations.)  

I recommend challenging TCO’s operations team should they insist that EES must maintain a minimum balance in your OBA. If you encounter any difficulties, please let me know and I will engage our external legal advisers again.

Kind regards,  
Laura Thompson  
Halcyon Mutual Bank  
</body>
